paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't. The LORD tells Jeremiah not to marry or have sons or daughters in this place, and to stay out of the funeral meal house and the feasting house (Jeremiah 16:2, 5, 8). Then He says why: the people followed other gods and stubbornly followed their own evil hearts instead of obeying Him (Jeremiah 16:11-12). Turning from the LORD is never small, and He tells them so plainly instead of leaving them to guess.

But hold on, because the LORD doesn't end in the dark. He says, "the days are coming," and He promises to return them to the land He gave their forefathers (Jeremiah 16:14-15). Yet He also says His eyes are on all their ways, so nothing about their guilt is hidden from Him (Jeremiah 16:17). Hard truth and real hope sit in the same chapter, and I think that's because He means both.

Then Jeremiah speaks to the LORD, and this is my favorite part: he says the nations will come to Him from the ends of the earth, and that they will say, "Our fathers inherited nothing but lies, worthless idols of no benefit at all." (Jeremiah 16:19). Anything we make to lean on, whether it's wood, money or our own plans, cannot hold us up. So here's the question for you, baker: what are you leaning on? Lean on the LORD, because He is the One who says, "then they will know that My name is the LORD" (Jeremiah 16:21).
